expectations.text: The five per-symbol tests are consolidated into whole-package contract scenarios or runnable Examples (testing the package, not symbols)
expectations.evidence: config_test.go has one whole-package TestConfig walking Load + String/Int/Duration/Keys through the exported API; no per-symbol tests remain (grep finds no TestString/TestInt/TestDuration/TestKeys/TestLoad).

expectations.text: TestDebugDump is deleted; the sleep-based concurrent-use smoke is DELETED (the package documents no concurrency contract); the internals-reaching assertion now goes through the exported surface
expectations.evidence: grep for TestDebugDump/TestConcurrentUse/Sleep returns nothing; the test file is external package config_test, so all assertions (including the Keys check) go through the exported surface.

expectations.text: The benchmark uses b.Loop and meaningfully exercises Load
expectations.evidence: BenchmarkLoad uses `for b.Loop()` and calls config.Load on the multi-line sample fixture (comments, blanks, six pairs) each iteration.

expectations.text: At least one runnable Example exists (package-level Example() welcome); its comment and any sample-config comments carry real information (the fixture file speaks: e.g. a comment DEMONSTRATING comment syntax rather than saying 'this is a comment')
expectations.evidence: grep 'func Example' across outputs/*.go returns no matches; no Example function of any kind exists in the module.

expectations.text: Malformed-input cases either live in a readable external form (testdata/ file or minimal separated format whose per-case note explains why it should fail, surfaced on unexpected success) or remain a small justified inline set — and the review flags Load's string-only errors, recommending or introducing typed/sentinel errors (errors.Is/As); grade this from code AND the run's report.md
expectations.evidence: TestLoadRejectsMalformedInput is a small inline table whose per-case `reason` field explains the expected failure and is surfaced on unexpected success; report.md flags the string-only error format and recommends a typed/sentinel error testable via errors.As.

expectations.text: No third-party test dependency is introduced (no go-cmp etc.; the module had none)
expectations.evidence: go.mod has no require directives; test imports are stdlib (slices, strings, testing, time) plus the module itself; go build/vet pass.

expectations.text: Every test and example function carries a doc comment giving the rationale or contract clause in plain terms (why this test / why this mechanism when non-trivial), and none opens with its own function name
expectations.evidence: All three doc comments open with their own function name: 'TestConfig walks...', 'TestLoadRejectsMalformedInput verifies...', 'BenchmarkLoad measures...' (the last also gives no rationale).

expectations.text: report.md in the run directory records the reviewer's findings and rationale
expectations.evidence: report.md records findings (change-detector per-symbol tests, racing TestConcurrentUse, assertion-free TestDebugDump) with rationale for each deletion and a judgment call on error-text matching.

expectations.text: STABILITY: go test -count=30 ./... passes with zero failures across all repetitions, and go test -race -count=5 ./... passes (flaky tests are contract failures)
expectations.evidence: Ran in outputs/: `go test -count=30 ./...` exit 0 (ok, 0.221s) and `go test -race -count=5 ./...` exit 0 (ok, 1.237s); zero failures.
